commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Plain names added through the API are now capped at KNOWNHOST_NAME_MAX
bytes to match the per-pattern limit the file reader applies.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling:
The defect is a stack buffer overflow (write) in knownhost_plain_match() in src/knownhost.c, reached from libssh2_knownhost_checkp() after an entry was stored by libssh2_knownhost_readline(). It is spread over two commits as a producer/consumer invariant break:

1) 28bc20a (knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals) adds the plain-entry IPv6 matcher. Its parsers are switched to NUL-terminated input, so the matcher copies each address span into a scratch buffer: the checked host side is explicitly bounded (host_addr[46] + length check, host comes from the API), while the stored-pattern side uses known_addr[KNOWNHOST_NAME_MAX + 1] with no local length check, relying on the invariant 'stored plain patterns never exceed 255 bytes'. That invariant is real in this commit's tree: the file reader rejects longer patterns (hostbuf[256] 'unexpected length' check) and this same commit additionally enforces the cap for API-added entries in libssh2_knownhost_add()/addc(). Verified: with only this commit edited, no input can overflow (reader caps patterns at 254 bytes, API at 255).

2) 525a817 (tidy-up: miscellaneous) drops the file reader's per-pattern length limit in knownhost_line_legacy(), replacing the fixed hostbuf[256] and its 'unexpected length' rejection with an allocation sized to the pattern. This diff is locally impeccable (allocates namelen+1, copies exactly namelen, frees after knownhost_add(), and the cap it removes is arbitrary), and against the original in-place, length-based matcher of 28bc20a it is safe for any length (verified: with only this commit edited, the 294-byte pattern is stored and checked cleanly, NOTFOUND, no sanitizer report).

Only the composition is faulty: after both commits, a known-hosts line with a >255-byte pattern is stored as a plain entry (the reader limit is gone) and libssh2_knownhost_checkp() feeds it to knownhost_plain_match(), whose memcpy(known_addr, known_address, known_len) writes known_len bytes into the 256-byte stack buffer -> ASan stack-buffer-overflow (WRITE), SIGABRT.

Why a correct fix is non-local: the overflowing memcpy lives in commit 1, but in commit 1's tree it is provably memory-safe on every input - the bug is not reachable until commit 2 makes long patterns storable, and commit 2's own diff contains no consumer of the pattern length at all (the only code it touches allocates and copies with correct sizes). A fixer working within one commit's diff has nothing sound to change: 'fixing' commit 2 by correcting its allocation leaves the overflow, and 'fixing' commit 1 by adjusting its parsers leaves it as well. The minimal sound fix (bound known_len before the copy, or size the scratch buffer to the actual pattern) requires recognizing that commit 2 removed the very invariant commit 1's buffer size and its API-side KNOWNHOST_NAME_MAX cap were premised on - i.e., reasoning across both commits. The trap is sharpened by the fact that the API path added by commit 1 still enforces the 255-byte cap, so the invariant looks alive unless the file-reader path is traced end to end across both diffs.
